text: This is a list of foreign cooking ingredients, and where to find them in Berlin. If something is missing, let me know. If you can’t find something, ask Found in… Berlin.

title: American cheese
text: American cheese, the square, “radioactive yellow” cheese that’s also known as Kraft Singles, can be found in the dairy section of most grocery stores.

title: Baking soda
text: Sodium bicarbonate is called Natron in Germany. It’s sold in small paper packets and boxes. You can find it in the baking section of all grocery stores. Look for the green Kaiser Natron boxes and packets. You can find Arm & Hammer baking soda at some Asian supermarkets.

title: Baking powder
text: Baking powder is called Backpulver in Germany. It’s easy to find. Look for small paper packets in the baking section of any grocery store. German baking powder is usually single-acting, while American and English baking powder is double-acting, and the difference is important. Broken English and many Asian markets have double-acting baking powder. If you are in a pinch, substitute double-acting baking powder with 1.25x the amount single-acting baking powder.

title: Boneless chicken thighs
text: Kaufland and Metro have them, and sometimes Penny. This is not a common product in Germany.

title: Brown sugar
text: German Rohrzucker or brauner Zucker is not the same as brown sugar. It does not contain molasses, and it will ruin any recipe that calls for brown sugar. Tate+Lyle sells light and dark brown sugar on Amazon. You can also find it in most asian supermarkets. Go Asia, Asia Markt Lee, Metro, Galeria Kaufhof and some Edeka stores have brown sugar. You can also make it yourself with sugar and molasses.

title: Caramelized condensed milk
text: LEDO supermarkets have caramelized condensed milk, and many other Russian staple foods.

title: Condensed milk
text: Condensed milk is called Kondensmilch. You can find it in the coffee section, next to coffee cream and H-Milch. It’s sold in small cans, or in small juice boxes. Condensed milk can be a false friend for people from the UK at least. If a recipe calls for condensed milk, you might want gezuckert Kondensmilch, also known as Mädchenmilch.

title: Corn tortillas
text: Corn tortillas are sold at Chili & Paprika and Aqui España.

title: Couscous spices
text: According to Quora, you can find Couscous spice at Galeria under the name Ras el-Hanout. Turkish markets and spice kiosks at Berlin’s many Wochenmärkte should also carry couscous spices.

title: Flour
text: North American all-purpose flour is the same as Type 550 flour in Germany. It’s in most supermarkets. Mehlstübchen has flours from all over the world, including Manitoba and type 00 dopio zero. Self-raising flour can be found at Galeria Kaufhof.

title: Graham crumbs
text: Graham crumbs are hard to find, but if you grind Leibniz crackers into crumbs, it’s exactly the same. You can find them in every supermarket.

title: Hot dog sausages
text: Most Turkish grocery stores have chicken and beef sausages. They taste exactly like the hot dog sausages in North America.

title: Kerrygold salted butter
text: Kaufland, Edeka, Lidl, Penny and REWE usually have Kerrygold salted butter.

title: Maple syrup
text: Most grocery stores have pure Canadian or American maple syrup. REWE keeps it close the the Nutella and peanut butter.

title: Marmite
text: Marmite is found at Galeria Kaufhof and Broken English. It was also spotted at Asia Mekong near Hackescher Markt and in the English section at Real,- and at KaDeWe.

title: Minced lamb
text: You can find it in Turkish supermarkets like Bolu or Eurogida. Find them with this map. Regular supermarkets and butcher shops do not sell it.

title: Molasses
text: Molasses is called Melasse in German. You can find it at Edeka and in many bio shops. You can also order it off Amazon.

title: Mustard powder
text: This staple ingredient of American BBQ can be found in most Wochenmärkte. I get mine from the Winterfeldtplatz market. Just look for Senfpulver at the spice kiosks. Colman’s Mustard Powder can be found at KaDeWe or ordered from Amazon.

title: Peanut butter
text: Most grocery stores carry peanut butter. REWE has both creamy and crunchy peanut butter. You will find it next to the Nutella. Go Asia has Skippy peanut butter.

title: Powdered sugar
text: Powdered sugar (also called confectioner’s sugar or icing sugar) is called Puderzucker or Staubzucker. It’s sold in small boxes in the baking section of all grocery stores. It’s very easy to find. There is a small difference between powdered sugar and confectioner’s sugar. If you need confectioner’s sugar, add 1 tablespoon of cornstarch per cup of powdered sugar.

title: Pumpkin puree
text: American Lifestyle KaDeWe Galeria Kaufhof You can also make your own. Supermarkets sell pumpkins when they are in season.

title: Sal de Guzano, sal de Chapulín
text: Chili & Paprika has agave worm salt and grasshoper salt.

title: Self-raising flour
text: You can get it from most Asian supermarkets, and at Galeria Kaufhof. You can make your own: add 2 teaspoons of baking powder for every 150g of flour.

title: Vanilla extract
text: Vanilla extract hard to find in Germany. I buy it on Amazon. Galeria Kaufhof, Chili & Paprika, Edeka and Metro also sell it.

title: Vegemite
text: Australia Shopping World has Vegemite. You can also order it from Amazon, but it’s more expensive.

title: Yeast
text: Yeast is called Backhefe in Germany. You can find it in small paper packets in the baking section of all grocery stores.

title: International
text: Galeria Kaufhof – Large selection of international products KaDeWe – Large selection of international products Mehlstübchen – Flours from all over the world

title: Eastern Europe
text: Kasatschok – Russian supermarket LEDO – Russian supermarket

title: Latin America
text: Aqui España – They have some Latin American products Chili & Paprika – Food from Mexico, Brasil, Colombia, Argentina, Peru La Bodega
